articles.title: Lewis Hamilton bought an 8,900-sq-ft Tribeca penthouse for $43.9 million; after a $57 million initial push, it sold for $49.5 million without him ever moving in
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton turned a $43.99 million New York property purchase into a multimillion-dollar gain without ever making the Tribeca penthouse his home.
articles.body: Lewis Hamilton turned a $43.99 million New York property purchase into a multimillion-dollar gain without ever making the Tribeca penthouse his home. The seven-time Formula 1 world champion bought Penthouse H at 443 Greenwich Street in 2017, then put the 8,908-square-foot triplex on the market for $57 million in 2019. After spending years on and off the market, the property entered a contract at $49.5 million in October 2021 and later closed at that price. Hamilton had already bought another Tribeca home at 70 Vestry Street, helping explain why the Greenwich Street property became an investment rather than a residence.What Did Lewis Hamilton Get For $43.99 Million At 443 Greenwich Street In TribecaHamilton bought Penthouse H from the sponsor for $43,991,455 in 2017. The triplex covered 8,908 square feet across three levels, making it the largest residence in the 443 Greenwich Street building. It also came with 3,246 square feet of private outdoor space and two parking spaces.The building itself was created from a former 19th-century bookbindery in Tribeca. Its private underground motor court and valet parking helped give 443 Greenwich Street its “paparazzi-proof” reputation. The setup allows residents to drive into the building rather than arrive through a busy street entrance. The Real Deal described the property as having an “paparazzi-proof” underground motor court when reporting on the building’s celebrity residents.That privacy was one reason the address became associated with well-known names. Justin Timberlake, Jessica Biel, Ryan Reynolds, Blake Lively, Jennifer Lawrence and Harry Styles have all been linked to the building at different times.For Hamilton, though, the appeal was not enough to turn the apartment into his New York home.What Features Made Lewis Hamilton’s 8,908-Square-Foot Triplex So ExpensiveThe size was only part of the story. The penthouse had six bedrooms, six full bathrooms and two powder rooms. A large great room had 20-foot ceilings, while original details from the old bookbindery were kept as part of the design. The residence also had multiple terraces and a private elevator serving the three floors.The upper terrace included a private plunge pool and summer kitchen. There were also two dedicated parking spaces, an especially valuable feature in Manhattan where private parking is limited.Residents of 443 Greenwich Street also had access to shared facilities. These included a 71-foot indoor pool, fitness facilities, a Turkish bath, a children’s playroom and a large rooftop terrace. Hamilton’s unit carried monthly common charges of about $18,360, according to its listing details reported by The Real Deal.The combination of space, outdoor areas, privacy and building services helped place the apartment among Tribeca’s most expensive homes.Why Did Lewis Hamilton Never Move Into His $43.9 Million Tribeca PenthouseHamilton’s most unusual decision was what he did not do with the apartment. He never moved into it.By 2019, he had another major property nearby. Hamilton bought a residence at 70 Vestry Street for about $40.7 million that year. The home measured roughly 6,500 square feet and included about 3,000 square feet of outdoor space.That purchase came before Hamilton’s 443 Greenwich Street penthouse was offered for sale. In February 2019, reports said the Greenwich Street property was being marketed for $57 million. The listing described it as a six-bedroom triplex, with a private elevator, pool, terraces and two parking spaces.The $57 million asking price was far above what Hamilton had paid two years earlier. The property later appeared on and off the market before the asking price was brought down. By October 2021, it had entered contract at $49.5 million.The sale also showed why Hamilton’s original purchase was not simply about finding a place to live. The penthouse had spent years as an asset in his property portfolio.How Did Lewis Hamilton Turn The 443 Greenwich Sale Into A $5.5 Million GainThe $49.5 million deal was still well below the original $57 million asking price, but it was more than Hamilton’s $43,991,455 purchase price. The difference was about $5.51 million before taxes, transaction costs and other expenses.The contract was handled by Compass broker Nick Gavin, and CityRealty listed the $49.5 million deal as the top residential contract in its October 2021 report. When the sale was completed, it was reported as the biggest residential sale in Downtown Manhattan that year.The buyer was initially hidden behind a Seattle-based entity. Later reports linked the purchase to Jennifer Gates, daughter of Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates. Gates was subsequently reported to be living in Hamilton’s former penthouse.So Hamilton’s New York property story ended with a simple but unusual result. He bought one of Tribeca’s largest and most private homes for almost $44 million, never moved into it, listed it for $57 million and eventually sold it for $49.5 million. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: PT Usha names Kumkum Mohod, Sujeet Kalkal as Team India’s MVPs after historic golds
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Teenage archer Kumkum Mohod and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal have been recognised as the standout performers of India’s campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Teenage archer Kumkum Mohod and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal have been recognised as the standout performers of India’s campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, with Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha naming them the inaugural recipients of the Jaspal Rana Award and Raja Randhir Singh Award respectively.The two awards have been instituted by the IOA to honour the best female and male sportspersons of the Games and commemorate the legacy of two stalwarts of Indian sport.Seventeen-year-old Mohod, making her Asian Games debut, won three medals, including two golds, while 23-year-old Kalkal produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of the Games to claim gold in the men’s 65kg freestyle wrestling category.India finished fourth in the medal standings with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals.Mohod ends South Korea’s long reignMohod was at the heart of one of the biggest breakthroughs for Indian archery in Aichi-Nagoya.Along with Ankita Bhakat and Kirti, she won the women’s recurve team gold, ending South Korea’s remarkable run of seven consecutive Asian Games titles in the event dating back to the 1998 Bangkok Games.Mohod then followed it with gold in the individual recurve event, ensuring that South Korea’s women failed to win a recurve gold at the Asian Games for the first time in the discipline’s history. Her individual triumph also secured a quota place for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Usha praised Mohod’s ability to deliver under pressure and drew a parallel with the late Jaspal Rana, after whom the award has been named.“It is fitting that Kumkum is the first recipient of the Jaspal Rana Award, as Jaspal too burst onto the scene as a prodigy at the 1994 Asian Games. Her composure under pressure and her ability to find her best form when her back was to the wall augur extremely well for Indian Archery,” Usha said.The IOA president believes Mohod’s breakthrough could finally help Indian archery cross a long-standing barrier at the Olympics.“India's archers have been knocking on the door for more than a decade now, and I firmly believe that this performance by Kumkum and her recurve teammates has shattered the glass ceiling for Indian archery. India came close to winning a maiden Olympic medal in the sport at the Paris Olympics, and I am convinced that the final frontier will be breached at the Los Angeles Olympics,” Usha added.Kalkal turns a lost final into goldKalkal, meanwhile, earned the Raja Randhir Singh Award after a gold-medal run that showcased his resilience and fighting spirit.The 23-year-old defeated reigning Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka of Japan in the semifinal before producing a stunning comeback against Abdulmazhid Kudiyev in the final.Kalkal trailed 2-9 with time running out but refused to give up, fighting back to win 10-9 in a dramatic finish. His triumph also continued India’s strong tradition in the 65kg category, following Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, who won Asian Games gold in the same weight class in 2014 and 2018 respectively.Usha said it was Kalkal’s refusal to accept defeat that made his performance particularly special.“Wrestling is India's sport, and Sujeet's performance will be spoken of for years to come. The gold medal will be celebrated, but his never-say-die attitude and refusal to accept silver have earned him a special place in the hearts of all Indians,” she said.“Winning gold medals in elite competition is not easy, but equally important is the effort that goes in when your back is against the wall. I wish Sujeet all success in the years ahead and will be rooting for him to deliver India's first-ever wrestling gold medal at the Olympic Games in two years' time.”The IOA will felicitate Mohod and Kalkal at a ceremony in the coming days.Their selection provides a fitting individual recognition to two athletes whose performances stood out in India’s 85-medal campaign.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shenzhen Open: Wu Yize wins first ranking title since he became world champion with 10-5 victory over Yuan Sijun
articles.summary: Wu Yize claims his first ranking title since he became world champion - a result that means China will have the top two players in the rankings for the first time.
articles.body:
Wu Yize secured his first ranking title since becoming world champion with a 10-5 win over Yuan Sijun in an all-Chinese final at the Shenzhen Open.

A profitable week for 22-year-old Wu pushes him to a career high of second place in the world rankings, behind Zhao Xintong.

It means that China has the leading two players in the rankings for the first time, further illustrating the country's position as a snooker superpower.

Wu became the second-youngest player to lift snooker's most coveted title at the Crucible when he beat Shaun Murphy in May, and he followed that up with a composed performance to see off surprise finalist Yuan at the Bao'an Sports Centre on Sunday.

Having demolished Judd Trump 6-1 in the semi-finals, Wu had early breaks of 117 and 80 to move 3-1 ahead against Yuan.

But, playing in his first ranking final, Yuan then reeled off three frames in a row.

Wu responded with two more half-centuries in the final frames of the opening session to take a 5-4 lead in the best-of-19 match.

Prospects of a tight final all the way to the finish line soon evaporated.

World champion Wu returned with breaks of 74 and 62 to take control at 8-5 in the evening session as Yuan struggled with his safety play.

And there was no way back for Yuan, 26, as Wu made sure of the trophy and the £177,000 top prize.

While Wu moves to second in the rankings, going ahead of Trump and Neil Robertson, Yuan jumps seven spots to 26th and earns £76,000.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: PM Modi congratulates Team India, hails ‘determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit’
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday congratulated the Indian contingent for its performance at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, praising the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday congratulated the Indian contingent for its performance at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, praising the athletes for representing the country with “determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit” as India concluded its campaign with 85 medals.India finished fourth on the medal table with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, ending the Games with its second-highest medal haul in Asian Games history. The tally was 21 medals fewer than the record 106 won at the Hangzhou edition in 2023.As the Games drew to a close in Nagoya on Sunday, Modi took to X to applaud the entire contingent and the medal winners while also expressing hope that the performances would help strengthen Indian sport at the grassroots level.‘Immense joy to the nation’In his post, the Prime Minister praised the athletes for their effort and sporting spirit throughout the continental showpiece.“As the Asian Games 2026 draw to a close, my compliments to every member of the Indian contingent for representing our nation with determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit. Congratulations to all our medal winners, whose performances have brought immense joy to the nation. May these Games inspire even greater achievements in the years ahead. May they contribute to strengthening sports at the grassroots too,” Modi wrote.The Prime Minister’s message came after more than two weeks of competition involving athletes from 45 countries. The Aichi-Nagoya Games witnessed a string of record-breaking performances, including 54 world records.The Games formally concluded with a spectacular closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya on Sunday.Historic golds and landmark performancesIndia’s campaign was marked by several historic performances and successful title defences across disciplines.Both Indian cricket squads retained their Asian Games titles, while the men’s and women’s kabaddi sides also won gold. The men’s hockey side successfully defended its title with a 5-1 victory over Malaysia, while the women’s team ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games gold by defeating China 1-0 in the final.There were also several breakthrough individual performances.Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games golf gold, while 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod created history by becoming the first Indian woman to win individual recurve gold at the continental showpiece.Mohod was also part of India’s historic women’s recurve team gold that ended South Korea’s seven-edition winning streak in the event. Wrestler Sujeet Kalkal, meanwhile, produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of the Games to win the men’s 65kg freestyle gold.Boxer Lovlina Borgohain also joined an elite group of Indian women by becoming only the second after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold.Looking beyond Aichi-NagoyaAthletics emerged as India’s biggest medal contributor with 24 medals, while shooting accounted for 15. Archery was the most successful sport in terms of gold medals, producing five top finishes.The campaign also provided a series of important milestones ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, with several young athletes making their mark on the continental stage.Earlier, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha named Mohod and Kalkal the inaugural recipients of the Jaspal Rana Award and Raja Randhir Singh Award respectively for the best female and male Indian sportspersons of the Games.With the Aichi-Nagoya campaign now complete, Modi’s message placed the emphasis not only on India’s medal tally but also on the broader legacy of the Games — inspiring another generation of athletes and strengthening the sporting ecosystem from the grassroots upwards.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: El fútbol colombiano vive una de las sorpresas más impactantes de los últimos años. El Barranquilla Fútbol Club, tradicionalmente reconocido como la cantera del Caribe y el lugar donde dio sus primeros pasos la estrella internacional Luis Díaz, se ha transformado en el verdugo oficial de los equipos históricos del país en la Copa BetPlay 2026. Pese a marchar en la parte baja de la tabla de posiciones en la segunda división (Torneo BetPlay), el conjunto atlántico ha mostrado una faceta implacable en el torneo que reúne a las instituciones de primera y segunda categoría: Fundado con el objetivo primario de foguear a promesas juveniles y servirse como plataforma hacia el profesionalismo —modelo del cual emergieron talentos de la talla de Luis Díaz, Teófilo Gutiérrez, Carlos Bacca y Luis Fernando Muriel—, el Barranquilla FC ha demostrado que la juventud no es sinónimo de inexperiencia al encarar partidos decisivos. Con la motivación por las nubes y el respaldo de la afición barranquillera, el cuadro rojo y verde no baja la guardia. En la siguiente fase de la Copa BetPlay 2026, el Barranquilla FC medirá fuerzas en los cuartos de final frente a otro histórico del fútbol colombiano: el América de Cali, recibiéndolo nuevamente en condición de local.

articles.title: Invasión de hinchas del Real Cartagena en el Jaime Morón: videos del caos
articles.standfirst: :Hnchas del Real Cartagena invadieron la cancha tras derrota ante Boca de Cali
articles.summary: :Hnchas del Real Cartagena invadieron la cancha tras derrota ante Boca de Cali
articles.body: Una jornada de fútbol que prometía ser decisiva en el Torneo BetPlay se transformó en un escenario de tensión, caos y desmanes en el Estadio Olímpico Jaime Morón León. El empate y posterior marcador adverso del equipo auriverde ante Boca Juniors de Cali desató la furia de un sector de la hinchada, culminando en la invasión del terreno de juego y serios enfrentamientos con la fuerza pública. La tensión acumulada en las graderías llegó a su punto de quiebre a la altura del minuto 68 del encuentro. La insatisfacción por el rendimiento futbolístico y el resultado en contra hizo que un grupo de barristas ubicado en la tribuna Sur vulnerara las vallas de seguridad e irrumpiera violentamente en el gramado. A los pocos minutos, simpatizantes ubicados en la sector Norte se sumaron a la invasión, obligando al cuerpo arbitral a suspender de inmediato las acciones y mandar a los jugadores de ambos equipos a refugiarse en los camerinos. El comité disciplinario de la Dimayor y las autoridades locales de Cartagena se encuentran evaluando los informes arbitrales y los videos de las cámaras de seguridad para determinar las sanciones correspondientes. La frustración acumulada de la afición por los constantes tropiezos en la lucha por el ascenso volvió a sobrepasar los límites de la convivencia deportiva. Ahora, el club heroico no solo enfrenta el impacto deportivo de perder puntos clave en el torneo, sino también las graves consecuencias administrativas y económicas de un episodio que ensombrece el fútbol en la Heroica.

articles.title: Los Golden Boys no dan opción en Rotterdam y dan otro golpe al ranking
articles.standfirst: Coello y Tapia revirtieron el gran inicio de Stupaczuk y Sanz para sumar su título 41 en la era Premier Padel por 6-3 y 6-2 volviendo a ampliar la distancia en el ranking sobre la pareja dos.
articles.summary: Coello y Tapia revirtieron el gran inicio de Stupaczuk y Sanz para sumar su título 41 en la era Premier Padel por 6-3 y 6-2 volviendo a ampliar la distancia en el ranking sobre la pareja dos.
articles.body: Los Golden Boys han vuelto a demostrar este domingo en la final del Rotterdam P2 por qué son la pareja dominadora del pádel moderno para sumar su título número 41 juntos en la era Premier Padel. Porque los Golden Boys no bajan el nivel. No aflojan. Si el resto quiere plantar cara, debe subir el suyo, pero ellos no entienden de descansos, torneos menores (por ranking) o semanas de asueto. Lo suyo es una carrera frenética en la que su naturaleza competitiva les obliga a ser, estar y demostrar que son los mejores. Porque en la inédita final del Rotterdam P2 partían como favoritos, pero ante una peligrosa pareja como Franco Stupaczuk y Jon Sanz que ya había demostrado las rondas anteriores que iban muy en serio esta semana, lucirían un domingo más su versión ganadora. Y además lo harían revirtiendo un inicio súper de sus rivales. Stupa y Sanz, extramotivados por el viento a favor de una actuación sobresaliente toda la semana, romperían de cara nada más saltar a pista y pondrían en tela de juicio el claro dominigio de la pareja uno que muchos esperaban. Pero sería un espejismo Como si de un aliciente más se tratara, verse por detrás en el marcador espolearía a los de Martín Canali para remar contracorriente y devolver el partido a esa lógica deportiva donde Tapia lleva la batuta y Coello toca lo justo y necesario para mejorar y potenciar una fórmula ya de por sí muy, muy buena. Del amago inicial de épica, al ya habitual dominio insaciable. Del 0-2 al 6-3 apenas pasaron 20 minutos, un espacio muy corto de tiempo en el que los Golden Boys igualaron, primero, rompieron después y definieron sin demasiada dificultad. Un cambio de patrón en la final que no por esperado dejaría descolocados a Jon y Stupa. La pareja hispano-argentina cuando nada a favor de corriente empasta bien, tiene muchos argumentos para ser una pareja dura y correosa, pero que cuando se ve tan lejos todavía demuestra que apenas está empezando a conocerse. Y, claro, ante Coello y Tapia no hay excusas. Si el primer set sería de un dominio aplastante tras la entrada en ritmo de los uno, el segundo sería el eco lógico que evidenciaría que ambas parejas están llamadas a cosas diferentes. Sanz no conseguía hacer daño a Coello en ese duelo de zurdos donde el de Valladolid suele verse más inseguro de lo habitual; y Stupa sostenía el intercambio con Tapia hasta que 'El Mozart' sacaba alguna genialidad de su infinito catálogo ya sea en el remate, la recuperación o la defensa. Con las dos opciones de rotura en contra de nuevo en el inicio del segundo set, Tapia y Coello demostrarían haber aprendido la lección para, primero, salvar un nuevo arreón rival y a continuación golpear de vuelta con dos quiebres consecutivos. Stupaczuk y Sanz sacarían adelante un servicio intentando la ilógica, pero la final ya había quedado vista para sentencia y tan solo esperaba que la última pelota cayera del lado que suele hacerlo en el pádel masculino desde 2023. El contrario al que ocupan Agustín y Arturo. Por 6-3 y 6-2 los Golden Boys sellaban su tercer año consecutivo proclamándose campeones en Rotterdam alargando, además, otro momento dulce más de la temporada tras la exhibición de París y en el que empiezan ya a poner muy cuesta arriba cualquier intento de remontada en ranking.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley Exits Eagles’ Week 4 Game vs Rams With Hamstring Injury on Second Carry
articles.summary: Saquon Barkley entered Week 4 as the main piece of a Philadelphia Eagles running game that had leaned on him through the first three weeks of the season. Phi...
articles.body:
Saquon Barkley entered Week 4 as the main piece of a Philadelphia Eagles running game that had leaned on him through the first three weeks of the season.

Philadelphia was already missing wide receiver DeVonta Smith and right tackle Lane Johnson against the Los Angeles Rams, leaving the offense with fewer proven options as it tried to handle another difficult matchup.

Saquon Barkley Leaves With Hamstring Injury

Barkley was injured on his second carry, a 6-yard run during the first quarter. He reached the sideline before slowing down and showing pain in the back of his right leg.

The Eagles sent Barkley into the medical tent for an initial examination. He then walked to the locker room. While Philadelphia initially listed him as questionable, the team officially ruled him out for the remainder of the game later in the second quarter.

Barkley did not return before halftime. He finished with two carries for 8 yards and one catch for 2 yards. The team did not immediately provide a timetable for his recovery.

The injury ended what had been a short afternoon for Philadelphia's leading running back. Barkley entered the game with 174 rushing yards on 34 carries, giving him an average of 5.1 yards per attempt.

He also caught three passes for 6 yards. Those numbers gave him 180 yards from scrimmage through three games and showed how important he remained to the Eagles' offense.

Philadelphia had other running backs available, but none offered Barkley's mix of speed, strength and experience. His exit forced the Eagles to change their approach while the game was still close.

Tank Bigsby Takes Over After Saquon Barkley's Exit

Tank Bigsby became the main running back after Barkley left. Philadelphia had listed Bigsby second on the depth chart, with Will Shipley available behind him.

Bigsby was asked to carry the ball, help in the passing game and keep the Rams from focusing only on quarterback Jalen Hurts. Shipley remained another choice if the Eagles needed fresh legs.

The situation became more difficult because Smith and Johnson were already unavailable. Smith missed the game with a hamstring injury, while Johnson was a late scratch due to personal reasons. Additionally, the shorthanded Eagles were missing several other critical starters, including tight end Dallas Goedert and linebacker Zack Baun.

Their absences had already taken away one of Philadelphia's best receivers and its starting right tackle. Barkley's injury then removed the player expected to lead the running game.

The Eagles could still turn to Bigsby and Shipley, but replacing Barkley was never going to be simple. Both backs had to take on bigger roles with little time to prepare.

Barkley's status will now be watched closely after the game. If he misses additional time, Philadelphia will immediately need its backup runners to carry a far heavier workload.

articles.title: Quinyon left the game with the Eagles leading 20-10
articles.summary: Quinyon Mitchell suffered an injury and is questionable to return as the Philadelphia Eagles deal with multiple injuries.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have managed to take control of their Week 4 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams , but the game has come at a cost. Philadelphia entered Sunday already missing several starters on both sides of the ball, leaving little room for further setbacks.

That became an even bigger concern during the game. With the Eagles leading 20-10, another key player has now been forced off the field, adding to an increasingly difficult injury situation for Philadelphia.

Quinyon Mitchell suffers knee injury and is questionable to return

Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (27). Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images.

Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell has suffered a knee injury and is questionable to return against the Rams, according to The Athletic's Zach Berman. The latest development leaves Philadelphia waiting to see whether one of its starting defensive backs can get back on the field before the game is over.

Berman reported on X: "Quinyon Mitchell has a knee injury. He's questionable to return."

Mitchell's injury comes after Philadelphia had already lost Saquon Barkley earlier in the game. The star running back exited after a six-yard run with a hamstring injury and was initially listed as questionable to return before later being ruled out.

The Eagles were already dealing with a lengthy injury list before kickoff. DeVonta Smith was inactive with a hamstring injury, Dallas Goedert remained out with a knee injury, Zack Baun was unavailable because of a concussion, and Marcus Epps was sidelined with a groin injury. Hollywood Brown and Fred Johnson were also inactive because of injuries.

Eagles face growing injury concerns while protecting 20-10 lead

Mitchell's potential absence is particularly important because Philadelphia's defense is already being asked to compensate for missing personnel. The Eagles entered the game without Baun and Epps, while the secondary now faces another potential loss with Mitchell being evaluated.

Philadelphia is trying to contain a Rams offense that welcomed Puka Nacua back into the lineup . The Eagles' official live tracker confirmed that Nacua was playing his first game of the season, giving Los Angeles another major receiving threat to deal with.

On offense, the Eagles have already had to adjust to life without Barkley, while DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert were unavailable from the outset. Tank Bigsby replaced Barkley after his injury, leaving Philadelphia to redistribute the workload in the backfield.

Philadelphia now has to monitor Mitchell while trying to preserve its 20-10 advantage. His questionable designation means a return remains possible, but another extended absence would leave the Eagles even more shorthanded as they attempt to close out the Rams.

With injuries piling up on both sides of the ball, Philadelphia's ability to maintain its lead could depend as much on the players still available as the advantage already established on the scoreboard.

articles.title: Los Angeles Chargers rule former FSU All-American inactive
articles.summary: Former FSU safety and Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James is inactive for their game against the Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers have made safety Derwin James inactive for their Week 4 game against the Seattle Seahawks, announcing the news Sunday on social media. He was listed as questionable on the team's injury report with a hamstring injury.

James started their first three games of the season and is tied for the team lead in tackles with 21. The veteran also has two quarterback pressures and one pass breakup. They signed him to a three-year, $75.6 million contract extension before the season, making him the highest-paid safety in the NFL for the second time in his career.

He is in his eighth year with the Chargers and is coming off his fifth All-Pro season and fifth Pro Bowl appearance. He has started all 101 of his appearances, recording 705 tackles, 19.0 tackles for loss, 40 tackles for loss, 12 interceptions, and six forced fumbles.

The Chargers have had a brutal start to the season, going 0-3 after entering the year looking to win the division and make a run in the playoffs. Their game against the Seattle Seahawks is set to start at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Landon Jackson injury: Bills defensive lineman limps off vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills defensive lineman Landon Jackson left Sunday's game against the New England Patriots with an apparent right leg injury.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills defensive lineman Landon Jackson left Sunday's game against the New England Patriots with an apparent right leg injury.

Jackson was injured with 2:29 left in the third quarter while rushing against Patriots left tackle Will Campbell. Jackson planted his right leg during the play and went down as Rhamondre Stevenson ran for 8 yards.

Jackson remained on his back after the play and took off his helmet. He then grabbed the helmet and slammed it against his left knee while appearing frustrated.

Bills athletic trainers tended to Jackson on the field before he eventually got up and limped to the sideline. He went into the blue medical tent for further evaluation.

Jackson's rookie season ended early in 2025 after he tore his MCL in Week 10 and was placed on injured reserve.

Jackson entered Sunday having appeared in three games this season with one start. He had seven tackles and one pass defensed.

Buffalo was already dealing with several injuries on defense. Ed Oliver was questionable to return with a knee injury, while Dee Alford was questionable with an ankle injury and Te'Cory Couch was doubtful with a hamstring injury.

2025 was a lost season for Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens . The two-time MVP missed four games and played hurt most of the other 13. He was clearly not himself behind center and Baltimore slumped to a 9-8 record that left the team outside the playoffs and longtime head coach John Harbaugh relieved of his duties.

2026 marked a comeback. Jackson's 9.8 yards per attempt were the highest in the NFL through three games for a 2-1 Ravens team. He was building on that sterling foundation in Week 4 against the overmatched Tennessee Titans . He had more than 200 passing yards and two touchdowns through 2.5 quarters in what looked to be a comfortable win.

While Baltimore continues to cruise, they've done so without Jackson. He left the game in the third quarter, ceding snaps to backup Tyler Huntley.

What's Lamar Jackson's status for Week 4?

Jackson is officially questionable to return. With the Ravens up by two possessions in the fourth quarter, he may remain on the sideline even if he's healthy enough to lead the Baltimore offense.

articles.title: Watch: 3 plays that proved critical in BYU’s victory over TCU
articles.summary: A bulldozing Bear, a pick, and a crucial tackle all played a hand in Cougars win.
articles.body:
Playing in wet circumstances that are more ideal for Frogs than Cougars, BYU (4-0, 2-0) leaped from TCU's Fort Worth pond with a clutch 17-10 victory on Saturday night to remain unbeaten in the Big 12.

In a game where big plays were hard to come by, BYU came up with three that helped turn the game in their favor and win at Ammon G. Carter Stadium for the first time in 20 years.

Motivated by his own frustration, BYU sophomore quarterback Bear Bachmeier engineered a 10-play, 72-yard scoring drive late in the fourth quarter, capping it with a 21-yard touchdown run right through the heart of the TCU defense.

Bachmeier bulldozed through the Horned Frog defenders similar to his 22-yard touchdown run last season to ice the game against Utah.

"I was playing so bad. I saw red when I was running the ball because I was so mad I just wasn't playing my game," said Bachmeier, who rushed three times for 40 yards on BYU's final drive. "But that is why there is a team and that's the culture at BYU. I love the guys. What a gritty and great team win."

Struggling to grip the ball in the rainy conditions, Bachmeier completed just 11 of 24 passes for 64 yards on a night when the Cougars lost star runner LJ Martin to an injury in the first quarter. The sophomore QB responded and produced 66 of his own rushing yards and a pair of touchdowns to improve to 16-2 as BYU's starting quarterback.

Going for it on fourth-and-4 at the BYU 35 early in the second quarter, TCU quarterback Jaden Craig made a critical mistake.

"I was just watching his eyes," said BYU safety Faletau Satuala. "Our defensive line was hitting home a lot, so I knew he was gonna have to get (the ball) out quick."

The charging Cougars chased Craig out of the pocket and he released the ball downfield, where Satuala was waiting.

"My receiver ran an in-route and (Craig) missed it," Satuala said. "He just threw it straight to me."

Satuala intercepted the pass at the 25 and ran 59 yards to the TCU 16 to set up Bachmeier's first touchdown run. His grab was the game's only turnover and it was also BYU's 45th interception since the start of the 2024 season.

Kalani Sitake teams are now 52-8 when they have a positive turnover margin.

Trailing 10-7 midway through the fourth quarter, TCU drove to the BYU 29. Facing third-and-10, Craig threw a short pass to Ed Small. The play had big potential until Cougar linebacker Cade Uluave pulled him down and held him to a 1-yard gain.

Uluave's tackle grew in significance when seconds later, Nate McCashland's 46-yard game-tying field goal fell a few yards short of the cross bar. The miss gave BYU the ball with 8:01 remaining and set up Bachmeier's touchdown drive to seal the victory.

"It was just a battle," said senior defensive tackle Keanu Tanuvasa. "It was a battle in the trenches — a war of who was going to be the nastiest team out there. We have trained for that. We have trained to play all four quarters, and we did a phenomenal job."

articles.title: Broncos complete a stunning comeback against the Rams with a 30-26 win
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos erased a 16-point halftime deficit to defeat the Los Angeles Rams 30-26 in a dramatic Sunday night thriller. Bo Nix delivered the winning...
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos turned a seemingly lost Sunday night into one of the wildest wins of the young NFL season, rallying from a 16-point halftime deficit to defeat the Los Angeles Rams 30-26 on Sept. 27.

Denver looked out of answers through the opening half, but quarterback Bo Nix and safety Talanoa Hufanga helped spark a dramatic turnaround. The Broncos scored 30 second-half points and improved to 2-1.

The Rams appeared positioned to close out the victory before Denver flipped the game late. Nix scored the go-ahead touchdown with 47 seconds remaining, and Hufanga intercepted Matthew Stafford in the end zone on the final play.

Los Angeles dictated the first half, limiting Denver to just 67 total yards while building a 16-0 advantage. Harrison Mevis supplied 3 field goals, while Tyler Higbee added a touchdown as the Rams repeatedly kept Denver's offense off schedule.

The Broncos struggled to create momentum before halftime, and the home crowd grew increasingly frustrated. Denver's offense could not produce a touchdown, while the Rams consistently found enough space to keep drives alive and control field position.

Matthew Stafford also appeared comfortable early, helping Los Angeles maintain its lead. The Rams entered halftime with control of the game, but the Broncos had another 30 minutes to change the direction of the contest.

Bo Nix sparks Denver's second-half rally

Denver's offense finally came alive after halftime, with Nix throwing touchdown passes to Pat Bryant and Nate Adkins. The Broncos followed both scores with successful 2-point conversions, quickly erasing the 16-point deficit and tying the game at 16.

The comeback did not arrive through one long scoring drive. Instead, Denver pieced together several important possessions while its defense began creating pressure and forcing Stafford into difficult decisions.

Nix's response was especially important after his quiet first half. He remained aggressive enough to make key throws while also contributing with his legs when Denver reached the goal line, setting the stage for an extraordinary fourth quarter.

With Los Angeles leading 19-16 in the fourth quarter, Hufanga delivered the game's biggest defensive play. He intercepted Stafford and returned the ball 66 yards for a touchdown, giving Denver its first lead at 23-19 with 4:49 remaining.

The play was especially significant because Hufanga had already missed opportunities to intercept Stafford earlier. Rather than letting those chances affect him, the safety stayed involved and eventually produced the turnover that changed the game's direction.

Hufanga was not finished after his pick-six. He recorded 5 tackles, 3 passes defensed, and 2 interceptions, earning a game ball from coach Sean Payton after one of the defining defensive performances of the night.

Los Angeles responded almost immediately after falling behind. Just 4 plays after Hufanga's pick-six, Stafford connected with Konata Mumpfield for a 48-yard touchdown, putting the Rams back in front 26-23 with the game entering its final minutes.

The touchdown showed why the Rams remained dangerous despite losing control of the momentum. Stafford had already produced several big completions, and Mumpfield's score restored Los Angeles' advantage when Denver appeared ready to finish its comeback.

Instead of folding after surrendering the lead again, the Broncos went back to work. Nix engineered a 65-yard, 10-play drive, making critical throws to move Denver into scoring position before delivering the decisive play himself.

Nix's winning drive included completions of 39 and 21 yards as Denver moved down the field. The quarterback then finished the possession with a 1-yard touchdown run, reaching over the goal-line scrum with 47 seconds remaining.

The score put Denver ahead 30-26 and completed a remarkable transformation from its first-half struggles. Nix finished with 17 completions on 34 attempts for 186 yards, 2 touchdowns, and 1 interception, while also scoring the winning touchdown.

Sean Payton praised the team's resilience after the game but acknowledged that Denver cannot continue relying on dramatic recoveries. The Broncos coach said he was comfortable with the team's fourth-quarter grit but uncomfortable with how it started games.

The Rams still had enough time to respond, and Stafford quickly moved Los Angeles downfield. He completed a 20-yard pass to Kyren Williams that took the Rams to Denver's 14-yard line before stopping the clock with 2 seconds remaining.

A false-start penalty then moved Los Angeles back to the 19-yard line. The Rams sent 5 receivers onto the field for the final play, leaving Stafford with one final chance to find an open target in the end zone.

That opportunity ended with another Hufanga interception. The safety secured Stafford's pass in the end zone as time expired, preserving Denver's 30-26 victory and preventing the Rams from completing their own late comeback.

Stafford produced 390 passing yards and 2 touchdowns, but he also threw 2 interceptions. Hufanga's pick-six and final interception turned those turnovers into decisive moments in a game where Los Angeles otherwise generated substantial offensive production.

The Rams also received strong contributions from their skill players. Davante Adams finished with 137 receiving yards, while Mumpfield recorded 93 yards and a touchdown. Kyren Williams added 158 scrimmage yards, but those performances could not overcome the late turnovers.

For Los Angeles, the defeat was particularly frustrating because the team held a 16-0 halftime lead and regained the advantage late in the fourth quarter. The Rams ultimately fell to 1-2, while Denver improved to 2-1.

Broncos turn another deficit into victory

The comeback continued Denver's remarkable early-season pattern. After losing 31-10 to Kansas City in Week 1, the Broncos have now won consecutive games, beating Jacksonville 20-13 before rallying past Los Angeles.

Sunday's victory also showed why Denver's defense remains capable of changing games even when the offense struggles. Hufanga's 2 interceptions provided the biggest moments, while the pass rush pressured Stafford in the second half.

Still, Payton's concern about slow starts remains relevant. Denver cannot assume every opponent will allow a 16-point deficit to disappear, making early-game execution an obvious area for improvement as the season moves forward.

Fun fact: Matthew Stafford entered the game with 17 fourth-quarter comebacks in the final 2 minutes, the most among active NFL quarterbacks .

Denver defeated Los Angeles 30-26 on Sept. 27.

Bo Nix scored the winning touchdown with 47 seconds left.

Talanoa Hufanga had 2 interceptions, including a 66-yard pick-six.

Matthew Stafford threw for 390 yards and 2 touchdowns but had 2 interceptions.

Denver improved to 2-1, while Los Angeles dropped to 1-2.

The Rams had one final chance, but Hufanga intercepted Stafford in the end zone.

LOS ANGELES (AP) — Lena Bilic will miss the upcoming season for defending national champion UCLA because of an ACL tear.

The school announced her injury on Sunday without providing further details.

The sophomore guard/forward from Zagreb, Croatia, averaged 3.0 points and 1.4 rebounds while appearing in 33 games and playing 12 minutes a game.

"We are devastated for Lena," coach Cori Close said in a statement. "She is such an important part of what we do here, and I know she'll continue to be impactful for us through her recovery."

articles.title: A (Semi) Statistical Recap of MTSU
articles.summary: Apparently football is much more fun when you don’t repeatedly give the ball to the other team. Who knew? Kansas gained 700 yards, rushed for 473, allowed 13...
articles.body:
Apparently football is much more fun when you don't repeatedly give the ball to the other team. Who knew?

Kansas gained 700 yards, rushed for 473, allowed 136, committed zero turnovers, and won 55-0. KU ran 83 plays, averaging 8.4 YPP. MTSU ran 42 plays, averaging 3.2 YPP. Kansas had 36 first downs. Middle Tennessee had seven.

Last time out, I wrote that the Kansas defense probably deserved to invoice the rest of the team for emotional damages. This week, the offense paid the bill.

After spending the first three games of the season giving us wildly different things to question about this team, the Jayhawks finally produced the kind of performance you would expect from a Power Four team playing a mediocre G5 opponent at home.

Actually, "the kind of performance you would expect" may be underselling it.

Consider: 700 yards of total offense is a school record. That's more than 2007 Nebraska (572). More than Wagner last year (631). More than Missouri in 1991 (648 in the Tony Sands game). More than Vanderbilt in 1985 (651). So KU didn't just set a school record on Saturday — the Jayhawks shattered it by 49 yards.

Kansas averaged 8.4 yards per play, picked up 36 first downs, rushed for six touchdowns, and scored on nine possessions. Middle Tennessee finished with seven first downs, 136 total yards, and nine punts. It was KU's first shutout since 2008 and the fewest yards Kansas has allowed in the Lance Leipold era. In fact, only three Kansas opponents since 1975 (my arbitrary cutoff for researching this) have gained fewer yards than Middle Tennessee's 136: Kansas State in 1992, Southeastern Louisiana in 2007, and Utah State in 1987.

Kansas is 2-2 heading into eight consecutive Big 12 games — with no byes — beginning next Saturday at #13 Utah. We still don't really know how much beating Middle Tennessee 55-0 tells us about what happens when Kansas starts playing teams like Utah, K-State, TCU, BYU, etc. But after what happened against Missouri and Arizona State, I'm willing to enjoy this one for a minute.

Kansas rushed for 473 yards — the fifth-highest single-game output in school history. The Jayhawks averaged more than eight yards per carry, and the concerning question of who would play behind Dylan Edwards after Yasin Willis' injury suddenly produced multiple answers.

Edwards looked perfectly comfortable as the feature back, carrying 20 times for 137 yards and three touchdowns. He also caught a 30-yard pass, giving him 167 yards from scrimmage. Isaiah Marshall was somehow even more efficient on the ground. He ran 11 times for 110 yards, averaging exactly 10 yards per attempt. Then there was Jalen Dupree.

Dupree entered the game with 13 carries this season. He nearly doubled that workload Saturday, rushing 12 times for 68 yards and a touchdown. His longest run went for only 15 yards, so it's not like there was one busted play inflating the numbers. He consistently found positive yardage and looked perfectly capable of handling meaningful snaps behind Edwards.

And then there was Khijohnn Cummings-Coleman. You may remember him from other positions, such as "safety."

Cummings-Coleman reportedly approached Lance Leipold after the Arizona State game about getting an opportunity on offense. Two weeks later, he carried four times for 48 yards and a touchdown and caught a 19-yard pass.

Kansas had six different players rush for at least 48 yards. This came one game after KU ran for 176 against Arizona State and three weeks after Missouri held the Jayhawks to 81.

So did I underestimate the Kansas offense?

The Missouri game still happened, and Middle Tennessee is not Utah. But the Arizona State game increasingly looks less like an offense incapable of moving the football and more like an offense that moved the ball pretty well and then repeatedly sabotaged itself.

Against MTSU, Kansas eliminated the sabotage. The result was the most total offense in school history.

Middle Tennessee's Santana Fleming returned consecutive second-quarter kickoffs for 38 and 52 yards. The second one gave the Blue Raiders the ball at the Kansas 45.

Fortunately, the defense responded by allowing two yards before forcing a punt. That makes this easier to brush off than the Arizona State game, when the Sun Devils returned the opening kickoff of the second half for a touchdown. It does not, however, make it less concerning.

Lance Leipold called kickoff coverage the biggest blemish afterward, and he's right. Kansas eventually adjusted and produced more touchbacks, but this is now something opponents have seen on film in consecutive games. Against Middle Tennessee, bad field position didn't matter. Against Utah, it certainly will matter.

There really isn't much else to complain about. Kansas didn't turn the ball over. It didn't allow a sack. Martin Connington made both field goals and all seven extra points. KU punted twice.

So we'll leave some manufactured outrage there.

Normally there are at least a couple of things to pick on KU about for this. But let's flip it upside down this week. Have you seen Middle Tennessee's offensive stat sheet?

What KU did to the Blue Raiders was impressive — MTSU finished with 136 total yards.

That is the fewest Kansas has allowed in the Lance Leipold era and, going back 50 years (again, my arbitrary research cutoff), only three KU opponents have finished with fewer: Kansas State in 1992, Southeastern Louisiana in 2007, and Utah State in 1987.

But Kansas didn't merely shut Middle Tennessee out. In fact, the Blue Raiders barely threatened to score. In 12 offensive possessions, the MTSU offense crossed midfield three times. Outside of the possession handed to them at the Kansas 45 by a 52-yard kickoff return, Middle Tennessee never ran a play inside the KU 40-yard line.

Middle Tennessee averaged 3.2 yards per play. They picked up seven first downs. They punted nine times.

Roman Gagliano, who entered the game with eight touchdown passes and one interception, completed 9-of-26 (34.6%) passes for 81 yards.

Cam'ron Lacy, who had caught a touchdown in each of MTSU's first four games, finished with two catches for 25 yards.

Former K-State RB Antonio Martin entered averaging 5.4 yards per carry with three 100-yard games. He finished with 40 yards. Thirty-four of those came on one play. Remove that run, and Kansas held Martin to six yards on his other seven carries.

Bam Crouch also returned after missing essentially the entire season so far following his shoulder injury four snaps into the opener. He finished with two tackles, but 1.5 were tackles for loss, including a third-down stop early in the game.

But this is also the second consecutive game in which KU's defense has been excellent. Arizona State managed 228 yards and 3.5 yards per play. Middle Tennessee followed with 136 and 3.2.

Whatever caveats we want to attach to the competition, that's a trend worth paying attention to.

Isaiah Marshall completed 13-of-22 passes for 161 yards and a touchdown. Those numbers are fine. His rushing numbers were considerably more interesting: 11 carries, 110 yards, 10 yards per attempt. Marshall wasn't sacked and didn't turn the ball over. That's probably the most important part.

Chase Jenkins went 3-for-3 for 65 yards in relief of Marshall and added 53 rushing yards and a touchdown. That's KU's backup quarterback producing 118 yards on six offensive touches. Totally normal stuff, right?

Dylan Edwards had himself a day, racking up 6.9 YPC on his way to 137 rush yards on 20 attempts with 3 TDs. He added just one reception, but for 30 yards.

Jalen Dupree had 68 yards and a TD on 12 rush attempts.

Khijohnn Cummings-Coleman had the aforementioned 48 yards and a TD on 4 rush attempts.

Donald Collier added 50 yards on 5 rushes.

Cam Pickett finally looked like an actual member of the Kansas offense after injuries basically erased the first three games of his season. He caught six passes for 49 yards, leading KU in receptions. Kansas already has Nik McMillan, Nahzae Cox, Bryson Hayes, and others capable of making explosive plays. If Pickett can become a reliable intermediate option for Marshall, that's another piece the offense hasn't really had available.

Speaking of Nahzae Cox , he caught two passes for 42 yards, including a 34-yard touchdown against his former team.

Bryson Hayes had three catches for 50 yards, highlighted by a 47-yarder.

Nik McMillan caught two passes for 30 yards.

Leroy Harris III , Corey Gordon , and Trey Lathan had 3 tackles each. Harris was also credited with a forced fumble and fumble recovery.

Martin Connington made field goals from 43 and 35 yards and all seven extra points.

Matthew Gill hit two punts for a 41.5 average.

At 9:15 PM Jayhawk time on Saturday, Oct 10, Kansas will travel to Utah for a late kick on the four-letter network. Things are about to get real.

articles.title: No. 1 Texas favored over Oklahoma in Red River
articles.summary: The Longhorns and Sooners square off in one of college football’s marquee games.
articles.body:
As the calendar officially turns to Red River Showdown week, the No. 1 Texas Longhorns are -9.5 favorites over the Oklahoma Sooners, according to FanDuel.

In the Longhorns' SEC opener, fans may have officially confirmed that the 2026 team will be led by its defense, rather than the offense as many predicted in the preseason. Colin Simmons led the defense with a school-record 5.5 sacks, bringing down Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon 10 times overall. Heading into the game, the Volunteers averaged 510 yards per game but managed just 221 total against the Longhorns' defense. The Volunteers rushed for just 70 yards against Texas in the contest, after putting up 298.67 yards on the ground in their first three games.

For comparison, the next week against Auburn, they rushed for 237 yards in a 24-14 win.

Oklahoma started the season and fooled everyone into thinking they had solved their offensive woes with a 51-0 drubbing of the UTEP Miners, but they soon crashed back to earth and showed the problems remained. They went to the Big House in Ann Arbor and turned in just 10 points — which was enough to tie the game in the fourth quarter. However, Bryce Underwood and the Wolverines did what many other teams had done before: they turned a John Mateer turnover into quick points to win.

Oklahoma avoided near disaster against New Mexico, holding a one-point halftime lead over the Lobos before taking advantage of one chunk play in the second half to escape with an eight-point win. However, their luck didn't hold in Athens, and the Georgia Bulldogs capitalized on four Oklahoma turnovers to come away with a 41-13 drubbing heading into their pre-Red River bye week.

Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian has owned the rivalry against Brent Venables, winning three of the last four with a whopping 136-46 scoring margin. In all three wins, the Sooners failed to score a touchdown and needed one with 15 seconds left to win.

All of that being said, one of the only things you can expect from this game is the unexpected, and none of the history actually matters, which is likely reflected by a line of less than 10 for an undefeated No. 1 team and a 2-2 team with its season goals on life support. This game generally hinges on which team survives the early emotions and takes better care of the football.

Either way, all eyes will be on Dallas as the two historic rivals line up in one of college football's greatest annual traditions.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Bills live updates: Score, news, discussion for NFL Week 4
articles.summary: The Patriots will try to make up some ground in the race for the AFC East on Sunday in Buffalo.
articles.body:
Having lost two of their first three games of the season, the New England Patriots are already looking up in the AFC East standings. The reigning division champions are trailing the 3-0 Buffalo Bills by a significant margin already, and are under pressure to start making up some ground even this early in the season.

They will have a chance to do so on Sunday, taking on these very Bills in a Week 4 meeting. However, the task at hand is a difficult one.

Not only are the Patriots coming off the worst loss of the Mike Vrabel era — a 35-6 shellacking at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars — they are also missing some core contributors in all three phases. Add the fact that they will be playing on the road, and you can see why Buffalo is favored to ultimately come away with a victory to further increase the difference between the two rivals.

Of course, the old "every given Sunday" adage still holds true. The last time the two sides met in Orchard Park under somewhat similar circumstances is a clear reminder of that. Could a repeat performance be in the cards today as well? Let's find out together.

Welcome to our Patriots-Bills live tracker and community discussion.

Sunday, Oct. 4, 1 p.m. ET | Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, NY) | Broadcast information | Inactives | Game day roster | Weather forecast

Joined by game day captain and ex-Bill Reggie Gilliam, the Patriots called called tails only to see the ceremonial coin come up tails. With Buffalo opting to start on offense, a short-handed New England defense missing the likes of Christian Gonzalez and Christian Barmore was up first. On the first series of the game, it did not matter: the home team went three-and-out with Kevin Byard breaking up a pass on third down.

Marcus Jones fumbled the ball on the ensuing punt return, but since a Bill had touched the ball before he did to pat it back into the field of play, the Patriots did retain possession.

Unlike its Buffalo counterpart, the Patriots offense did manage to move the chains on its initial possession of the game. A Drake Maye scramble and passes to tight ends Eli Raridon and Hunter Henry gave the unit some breathing room after starting at its 3-yard line. New England did face a 4th-and-3 in Buffalo territory, but Maye connected with Romeo Doubs to move the chains. One play later, the pair connected again on a 14-yard touchdown pass — capping a 12-play, 97-yard drive in style. | Patriots 7 : 0 Bills

The Patriots defense started its second series with a 4-yard Elijah Ponder sack of Josh Allen, but Buffalo managed to keep the series alive despite subsequently facing third or fourth down three different times — knocking on the door as the first quarter came to a close.

After converting a 3rd-and-6 to start the second quarter, the Bills found the end zone on an 8-yard James Cook run to even the score. | Patriots 7 : 7 Bills

The Patriots offense got a gift to start its second drive, with Bills kicker Tyler Bass sending the kickoff after his team's touchdown short of the landing zone. However, the unit failed to capitalize even though it found himself on the Buffalo side of the field again after a TreVeyon Henderson reverse for 10 yards. Unfortunately for New England, though, the series – as has been the case too often this year – ended with a turnover: a Drake Maye strip sack was recovered by the Bills.

Just like the Patriots before, the Bills were unable to take advantage of the gift they received. They quickly went three-and-out to punt the ball back to New England's Marcus Jones, who gained 17 yards on the runback to give his team possession on the 37.

Things seemingly continued to go downhill for the Patriots on the next drive, but what was initially ruled a Drake Maye fumble returned by the defense for a touchdown was overturned and called incomplete after a brief review. Instead of disaster striking, the team answered by gaining 26 yards on a pass to Mack Hollins and another 10 on a Rhamondre Stevenson run. Maye then added another 26 on a scramble to bring his team to the 1-yard line. Stevenson capped the series out of a jumbo look one play later to put his team up again. | Patriots 14 : 7 Bills

The Patriots defense spoke all week about defending the "second play" against Josh Allen, but it failed to do so on Buffalo's next drive after the Stevenson touchdown. The former league MVP bought some extra time on a 50-yard pass to Khalil Shakir, who managed to break a tackle before gaining the final 29 yards to set up his team on the New England 6 just outside the two-minute warning. Unfortunately, an apparent stop on third down was overturned by a holding penalty against Marcus Jones, which in turn was followed by head coach Mike Vrabel getting flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct. This gave the Bills second life, and they cashed in three plays later to tie the game again. | Patriots 14 : 14 Bills

With a minute remaining in the first half, the Patriots offense had an opportunity to carry some momentum into the half. However, the unit opened with two incompletions followed by pressure off the left side forcing an errant throw on third down. The subsequent Mitch Wishnowsky punt left the Bills with 29 seconds left on the clock.

The Bills did not take long to move back into Patriots territory on their next drive, gaining 22 yards on a first-down pass from Josh Allen to Keon Coleman. However, Carlton Davis knocked the ball out of Khalil Shakir's hands on the very next play — with teammate Elijah Ponder recovering it turned into a potentially points-saving play on the edge of field goal range.

What followed, however, was a bad break for the Patriots. Romeo Doubs failed to haul in a Drake Maye pass on the first play after the interception, and the ball popped in the air only for the Bills' Dee Alford to intercept it and run it back to the New England 9-yard line with 5 seconds on the clock. Tyler Bass hit a field goal just before time expired, giving Buffalo its first lead of the day. | Patriots 14 : 17 Bills

The Patriots were mostly driving the ball well in the first half, and they stared the second in the same fashion. A toe-drag by Romeo Doubs on the sideline and a Drake Maye scramble brought the offense back into Bills territory. Once there, Maye hit Hollins for a gain of 19 and later connected with Doubs again to convert a 4th-and-2. However, despite finding themselves at the Bills 2-yard line, New England had its fair share of trouble actually pushing the ball in — until Maye hit Doubs on a 2-yard goal line fade for six. | Patriots 21 : 17 Bills

New England's defense delivered a stop on its first series of the second half. After nothing but short gains, Carlton Davis came flying down on a screen attempt on 3rd-and-8 to bring Keon Coleman down for a modest gain of 1 yard, prompting the Bills to punt.

The Patriots fared better on their next possession, preventing a three-and-out on a toe-drag sideline catch by DeMario Douglas. However, the series did not advance much further after that and eventually Mitch Wishnowsky had to come out for his second punt of the day.

The Patriots defense continued to put the clamps on Josh Allen and the Bills offense on the next play, nearly taking the quarterback down for a safety when Gabe Jacas powered through left tacke Dion Dawkins. Allen prevented that particular outcome, but couldn't stop his team from going three-and-out a second straight drive.

Trying to go ground-and-pound, the Patriots called on Rhamondre Stevenson three straight times to open their next possession. But while he gained 8 yards on his first carry, the offensive line failed to create a significant push on the next two plays. The result: a net gain of 0, and another punt.

Buffalo's run game showed some signs of life in the early fourth quarter, with James Cook gaining a combined 35 yards on the first three plays of the series. The Bills did run out of steam eventually, but not before a Keon Coleman 21-yard grab over cornerback Kindle Vildor — entering the game for an injured Charles Woods — put them in field goal range. A Marcus Jones open-space tackle on third down prevented further damage, but the home team still cut into New England's lead. | Patriots 21 : 20 Bills

articles.title: Ronaldo-less Portugal beat Norway 2-1 to reach Nations League quarterfinals
articles.summary: Holders Portugal first team to qualify for 2026-27 UEFA Nations League despite Cristiano Ronaldo’s absence.
articles.body:
Portugal defeated Norway 2-1 on Sunday, without superstar striker Cristiano Ronaldo, to qualify for the UEFA Nations League quarterfinals.

Goncalo Ramos secured victory for Jorge Jesus’s Portugal in the Group A4 clash after Joao Cancelo’s rocket levelled Kristoffer Ajer’s stunning opener for Norway.

Portugal played out the final minutes with 10 men after Francisco Conceicao was dismissed for two yellow cards in the space of a few seconds for dissent following his unsuccesful appeal for a penalty.

Former Real Madrid and Manchester United striker Ronaldo walked out on the squad on Wednesday, ahead of the previous game against Denmark, after Portugal’s all-time top goalscorer learned he would not start.

Portugal are now guaranteed to finish in the top two spots in the group, thus granting them passage to the last eight in March 2027.

Norway took the lead in Porto against the run of play with a stunning effort from Brentford defender Ajer after 36 minutes.

The Norwegian met a bouncing ball on the edge of the box perfectly and bent it into the top corner.

However, two minutes later, Barcelona defender Cancelo scored a similarly superb goal, rifling home from about 20 yards.

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland fired across the face of goal after an hour and was replaced by Jorgen Strand Larsen a few minutes later.

Nations League holders and two-time record champions Portugal nosed in front when AC Milan striker Ramos, starting in place of Ronaldo, tucked home from close range after being teed up by Joao Felix.

Conceicao’s foolish dismissal left Jesus’s team in a tough spot for the final few minutes, but they held on to triumph for the fourth time in four games in the group.

images.caption: Portugal's Goncalo Ramos celebrates scoring his side's second goal against Norway in the UEFA Nations League [Reuters]

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts 2026 results: Luke Humphries beats Gerwyn Price
articles.summary: World number two Luke Humphries ends a 16-month wait for a PDC major trophy with a stunning 6-4 victory over Gerwyn Price in the World Grand Prix final.
articles.body:
World number two Luke Humphries ended a 16-month wait for a PDC major trophy with a stunning 6-4 victory over Gerwyn Price in the World Grand Prix final.

Humphries, 31, was at the top of the sport two years ago but has found his dominance superseded by Luke Littler and had failed to taste major success since winning the Premier League in May 2025.

A ranking title had eluded him since claiming the Masters in February last year, but he showed his class and an abundance of character to lift the title at the unique 'double-in, double-out' tournament in Leicester.

The second seed, who was in a record-breaking fourth successive World Grand Prix final, trailed Price 3-0 but won four sets on the spin to take control.

Price levelled but Humphries broke in the deciding leg of set five and then won three straight legs to be crowned champion.

It is his second World Grand Prix title, adding to his 2023 success that started his march to becoming world number one.

The victory ensures he retains his number two ranking from the Netherlands' Gian van Veen.

"It's kind of like I needed this to give me a bit of confidence," Humphries told Sky Sports.

"It's been a torrid 15 or 18 months, losing so many major finals. I felt like I had not much to give tonight."

Defeat for Price means his four-year wait for a major PDC title continues, while he has now lost five successive major finals, including three this year.

World Grand Prix: Brilliant Humphries fights back to beat Price - as it happened

Darts' World Grand Prix: Results and prize money

Price, who was playing in a fourth Grand Prix final, claimed the first set with a stunning 132 three-dart average.

He raced into a 3-0 lead and Humphries admitted afterwards that avoiding a 6-0 clean sweep was on his mind such was the brutality that Price was producing.

The fourth set saw the momentum swing however. With Price waiting on tops to move to within two sets of victory, Humphries nicked it by taking out a brilliant 105, with what he said "felt like the biggest shot of my career".

From there his levels started to rise and he claimed the following three sets to lead.

Price rallied in set eight and won three successive legs to force a best-of-three finale, but, after a short break, Humphries found another gear.

Set nine went to a deciding leg, but unlike the previous four sets in the match where that had happened, there was a break of throw, with Humphries finishing in 10 darts.

That left Price dejected and Humphries won three unanswered legs to claim a ninth major PDC title.

"The sport is in such a special place that when you pick these trophies up they mean a lot more," said Humphries.

"When I was winning, I don't think there were so many good players. I'm happy to win a couple a year - one a year is great.

"To go on and win like I did is going to be tough. I don't think I can't do it, I'm just trying to pick up as many titles as I can.

"I worked incredibly hard, showed a lot of grit and determination. I think these are a lot sweeter than the ones you win with ease."

articles.title: Ireland refuse handshake with Israel and don armbands in Nations League tie
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland football players again wear black armbands and refuse handshakes with Israel in UEFA Nations League.
articles.body:
Ireland players again wore black armbands in recognition of Palestinians killed in Gaza and bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem before the teams’ second UEFA Nations League football match on Sunday.

The League 3 Group B match ended in a 1-1 draw and, despite being played behind closed doors and on neutral ground, was once again played out in a confrontational manner.

Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher stepped in as captain for Dara O’Shea, who was excused to be with his wife for the birth of their child, and pointedly avoided shaking hands with Israel captain Dor Peretz, despite completing the usual pre-match formality with the referee and one of his assistants.

Kelleher’s action was a repeat of O’Shea’s, who refused to shake Israel captain Manor Solomon’s hand before the first match in Debrecen, Hungary, last week. Ireland went on to win that game 3-0 through three first-half goals.

Solomon was dropped to the bench for Sunday’s match in Backa Topola, Serbia. Israel forward Sayed Abu Farchi was back in the squad after serving a suspension for getting sent off following his gun-simulation goal celebration during Israel’s 3-1 defeat to Austria on September 25.

Finn Azaz, whose mother has Israeli heritage, was among the Irish substitutes after playing from the start against Austria on Thursday.

Troy Parrott’s penalty in the 39th minute, after a foul by Peretz on Jimmy Dunne, gave Ireland a 1-0 halftime lead. A disagreement also broke out on the sidelines as the players made their way off the field for the interval, although the referee quickly intervened.

Peretz secured a point for Israel with a poked effort from close range in the 47th minute.

Sunday’s game was initially supposed to be played in Dublin, but the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) moved it to a neutral venue for “operational reasons” in June following widespread calls for a boycott in protest of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. The FAI said the game would be played with no fans present.

It followed the FAI’s motion the previous November calling on UEFA to ban Israel from club and international competitions.

All the Irish players had been under pressure from home – where affinity with Palestinians is strong – to boycott the second match against Israel, though the pressure was greater during the first game.

“I felt that pressure growing day by day, and it’s getting almost to a breaking limit now,” Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said at the time.

Ultimately, only reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu decided to skip both of the contentious games, saying in a statement that it was his “personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong”.

More than 160 Irish sportspeople had signed an open letter urging the FAI to reconsider its decision to go ahead with the two games.

Before the departure for Hungary, people protested outside the team hotel in Dublin for the players to boycott the matches. The SIPTU trade union displayed a huge poster in central Dublin beside the River Liffey asking the players to “Go with your conscience!” and “Don’t play with genocide” beside an image of a blood-splattered ball.

Former Ireland coach Brian Kerr said the FAI had “lost the respect of the Irish people” for going ahead with the games.

But the FAI argued UEFA could sanction the team. Ireland is cohosting the 2028 European Championship with England, Wales and Scotland.

Protesters threw tennis balls with Palestinian flags onto the field during Ireland’s 2-2 draw with Austria on Thursday. A man with a Palestinian flag also tried running onto the field.

On Saturday, an Israeli journalist stated during the pre-match news conference that the Irish players had called the Israeli players “monkeys” during last week’s game, leading to an immediate rebuke from Irish communications officer Kieran Crowley, who said it was “a lie” and ended the news conference.

The players had only decided to go ahead with the fixtures after a dramatic day in Debrecen before the first match, when both the news conference and training were delayed for hours while they deliberated. They reportedly voted 14-8 in favour of continuing after Bazunu’s withdrawal that morning.

Ireland’s national broadcaster RTÉ was only providing stripped-back coverage of both games against Israel to meet contractual obligations. There was no studio presentation, commentary on the international feed, or analysis. RTÉ said it was not accepting advertising or sponsorship around either game.

RTÉ also recently announced that Ireland will boycott the Eurovision Song Contest for a second year due to Israel’s participation.

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries beats Gerwyn Price 6-4 after epic comeback to claim major title in Leicester
articles.summary: Luke Humphries recovered from three sets down to beat Gerwyn Price and win the World Grand Prix title for the second time in four years; Humphries avoid a third consecutive runner-up finish at the double-in event, as Price extends his wait for another TV major
articles.body:
Humphries, the first player in history to reach the final four years running, rallied from 3-0 down to reel off six of the next seven sets at the Mattioli Arena in Leicester and claim a first major title of the year.

The former world champion posted a 93.16 average and fired 10 maximums in a topsy-turvy contest, where Price had early control before Humphries landed a 105 finish in a deciding leg of the fourth set to avoid falling further behind.

That checkout sparked a run of four consecutive sets from Humphries, who capitalised on Price missing set darts for a 5-4 lead by winning five straight legs and closing out an impressive victory.

It's the second time in four years that Humphries has beaten Price in the World Grand Prix final, following on from his 5-2 win in 2023 , with the Englishman claiming the £150,000 first prize and extending Ice Man's wait for another TV major.

How Humphries claimed comeback win over Price

Price required just 34 darts to wrap up an extraordinary first set in straight legs, posting 12-dart holds either side of opening with six perfect darts on his way to breaking Humphries with a 10-darter.

Humphries got his first leg on the board early in the second but missed three darts to break Price, who punished him before taking out 101 and 82 on his way to opening a two-set advantage.

Price took further control by breaking Humphries with another 101 outshot in the third, where his opponent took out 109 to save the set before watching the Welshman extend his lead in a final-leg decider.

Humphries needed a string of clutch doubles to avoid being cut further adrift in the fourth, as he responded to Price nailing a 130 checkout on the bullseye by sealing his first set with a 105 finish in the last.

Momentum flipped further Humphries' way when he went on a four-leg run to close out the fifth and edge ahead in the sixth, where Price posted 99 and 94 finishes before Humphries broke back and closed out the set.

A shell-shocked Price fell behind for the first time when Humphries landed an 11-darter on throw and broke in the next leg, with the Englishman continuing to improve as he wrapped up a fourth consecutive set on double 16.

Price levelled by breaking in a scrappy opening leg and sweeping the eighth set, with 2020 champion leading in the ninth but wasting two set darts to move a set from victory.

Humphries took full advantage by breaking Price and then edging ahead with an extraordinary 10-darter, before accelerating to the victory line by racing through the next set in straight legs and wrapping up victory with an 11-darter.

Price rues missed chances as Humphries celebrates 'special' win

Luke Humphries , who becomes only the fourth player to win multiple World Grand Prix titles:

"This is really special, getting that barren major run off my back. I think the biggest shot of my career was the 180, 105 outshot in the fourth set, as if Gezzy [Price] goes 4-0 up then it's game over. Then at 3-1, I relaxed.

"I feel I deserved a major. Maybe I didn't tonight as Gezzy was maybe the better player but I worked hard and showed grit and determination.

"A win like that is sweeter than when you win with ease. I am looking forward to taking the trophy home to my son so he can see his dad not have a runners-up one!"

Runner-up Gerwyn Price , who remains without a major title since the 2022 World Series Finals in Amsterdam:

"I don't want to win a major, do I?! Luke [Humphries] played brilliantly in the middle part of the game but I still squandered opportunities to put him under pressure, too many opportunities.

"It was a fantastic game and it was whoever took their opportunities. I missed quite a few at crucial times. I am gutted to lose another major final but I will get over it - I am bothered! "

Mardle: Humphries didn't succumb under pressure

"Humphries was in trouble, then a bit more and then a bit more - so to get out of it was an incredible effort. The last two sets were his best. He was under the cosh for more than an hour but didn't succumb. He stood up to everything Gezzy threw at him, which was a lot!

"When you have won before, which Luke has done many times and in many, ways, there is that belief of, 'I'm under pressure, but let's just see as I know my game can win', rather than 'oh no, I am going to get beat'. He played his game and he won.

"Gezzy tightened up after a great start. He says things in the spur of the moment but the way he competes, he wants it. You can't play like he did this evening if you don't care!

"It is disheartening and disappointing when you are 3-0 up and don't win, but he has lost enough finals to know nothing is a given. He is still a young man and will get many more opportunities. He knows he is good enough."
